title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and August 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for August 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF Portwatch differs from alternative sources.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

This chokepoint handles about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade, directly influencing Brent crude benchmarks, tanker charter rates, and energy supply volatility. Trader consensus on related Polymarket contracts reflects persistent uncertainty around full normalization, with any sustained diplomatic de-escalation or verified volume spikes serving as key swing factors ahead of year-end resolution thresholds.

eventMetadata.context_description: The tight race for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination centers on Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Vice President J.D. Vance, whose near-even market prices reflect trader views of shifting coalitions within the party after the prior cycle. Both draw from overlapping yet distinct bases, with Kennedy's cabinet role in health policy and Vance's position as sitting vice president providing institutional footholds. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's climb to third place stems from his foreign policy record and donor networks, preventing early separation at the top. Historical patterns show early leads often narrow once primary focus shifts to electability and records. Upcoming catalysts such as 2026 midterm results, candidate announcements, and Senate dynamics could widen gaps, underscoring the uncertainty captured in current pricing.

title: Toronto Blue Jays vs. Houston Astros
description:

This market will resolve to "Toronto Blue Jays" if the Toronto Blue Jays win the game.

Other named figures, including regional officials and opposition figures, register minimal implied probability due to the ruling party’s structural dominance and the absence of viable succession mechanisms or challenges within the current political framework. Shifts remain possible through unforeseen health events, major internal party fractures, or sudden escalations in ongoing regional conflicts, though none have materialized in the post-election period.

eventMetadata.context_description: US-Iran hostilities, rooted in the 2026 conflict over Iran's nuclear program, ballistic missiles, and control of the Strait of Hormuz, have featured repeated short-term pauses since the April two-week ceasefire brokered by Pakistan. The June memorandum of understanding established a 60-day window for a broader deal that collapsed in early July after Iranian strikes on commercial vessels prompted US retaliation and President Trump's declaration that the truce was over. As of early August, the US has paused major airstrikes following weeks of escalation, while mediators including Pakistan, Qatar, and Oman advance proposals for renewed 10-day or similar pauses to revive talks on shipping access, sanctions relief, and nuclear constraints. Trader assessments reflect this fragile diplomatic window, with outcomes hinging on whether low-level incidents resume or both sides sustain the current operational halt long enough for substantive negotiations.
